asset_specifications.power_curve_characteristics: Low specific power optimized curve rising between 3.0 and 10.5 m/s, flat plateau at 50.0 MW between 10.5 and 25.0 m/s

regulatory_framework.regulation_name: MERC (Forecasting, Scheduling and Deviation Settlement for Solar and Wind Generation) Regulations

mechanics.over_forecast_rule: If Schedule > Actual + 5.00 MW, generator pays DSM penalty on excess deviation (Schedule - Actual - 5.00 MW)
mechanics.under_forecast_rule: If Schedule < Actual - 5.00 MW, generator pays DSM penalty on shortfall deviation (Actual - Schedule - 5.00 MW)
mechanics.symmetric_penalty: Both over-predicting and under-predicting beyond 5.00 MW trigger financial penalties under MERC.
mechanics.calculation_formula: Penalty (INR) = Deviation_MW * 1000 kW/MW * 0.25 hours * Rs 3.275/kWh * Slab_Multiplier

regulatory_framework.scheduler_directive: Maintain schedule strictly within Actual ± 5.00 MW. Never over-cut forecast to create shortfall penalty; never inflate forecast to create excess penalty.

regime_1_nocturnal_low_level_jet.meteorological_driver: Deccan Plateau nocturnal boundary layer stabilization and Low-Level Jet (LLJ)
regime_1_nocturnal_low_level_jet.generation_behavior: Strong, continuous, steady nocturnal generation. Night and early morning is prime power generation period.
regime_1_nocturnal_low_level_jet.scheduling_rule: NEVER set night blocks to 0.0 MW. Keep schedule anchored to 20-40 MW based on NWP hub-height winds.

regime_2_morning_breakdown.meteorological_driver: Solar sunrise and initial boundary layer convective mixing eroding the nocturnal inversion
regime_2_morning_breakdown.generation_range_mw: Steep decay from ~23.5 MW down to ~17.5 MW
regime_2_morning_breakdown.generation_behavior: Orderly downward ramp as surface warming decouples the nocturnal jet.
regime_2_morning_breakdown.scheduling_rule: Track downward ramp step-by-step (~2.5 MW/hour). Do not lag the decay to prevent over-forecasting penalties.

regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.meteorological_driver: Intense solar heating, deep turbulent boundary layer friction dissipating wind velocity
regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.generation_range_mw: 12.0 to 17.0 MW (with diurnal trough at 13.17 MW between 17:00 and 18:00)
regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.generation_behavior: Suppressed generation during daylight hours; light wind floor supported at 6.0 MW.
regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.scheduling_rule: Maintain realistic daytime baseline (12-16 MW in moderate winds, 6.0 MW floor during calm spells).

regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.meteorological_driver: Ground radiative cooling, thermal boundary layer collapse, and sudden onset of nocturnal LLJ
regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.generation_range_mw: Upward surge from 13.2 MW to >19.0 MW
regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.generation_behavior: Boundary layer re-stabilization and jet reconstitution.
regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.scheduling_rule: Initiate upward ramp at 17:45-18:15 IST to prevent under-forecasting penalties.

operational_rules: Rule 1: Maharashtra MERC 10% (5.00 MW) Two-Sided Band Mandate. Zero penalty corridor is [Actual - 5.00 MW, Actual + 5.00 MW]. Avoid both excess (>+5.00 MW) and shortfall (<-5.00 MW).
Rule 2: 24-Hour Continuous Operation. Wind produces power day and night. Nighttime is peak production (20-42.5 MW). Solar zeroing rules strictly forbidden.
Rule 3: Vertical Wind Shear Scaling. Hub height 130m is significantly windier than 10m surface or 100m NWP outputs. Scale winds using Hellmann power-law alpha = 0.143.
Rule 4: Evening Ramp Timing. Anticipate the 17:45-18:30 surge.
Rule 5: Revision Schedule Synchronization. Follow exact 16 intra-day revisions (every 90 min from 01:15 to 23:45, effective with 45 min lag from 02:00 to 00:30).
